name: Dawnbreak Australia
finding: Dawnbreak was ALWAYS paid from the very first event. Founded by Jian in early 2024, who had previously run a free community cold water dip club called 'Cold Nips' in Western Australia for 5 years. The silent disco concept came from an accidental beach dance party that got noise complaints from council and residents. A friend suggested doing it as a silent disco. The very first Dawnbreak event was on the Gold Coast with ~35 attendees, and it was ticketed. Current ticket prices are ~$34.90 AUD + booking fees. Cold Nips (free morning swims) and Dawnbreak (paid silent discos) are separate ventures. The user's belief is CORRECT: the free morning swims (Cold Nips) were a separate community, and the silent disco events were always paid. Revenue model = paid ticket events with headset rental baked into the ticket price. Uses Humanitix (charity-focused ticketing platform where 100% of booking fee profits go to charity). Sold out their entire 2025 Australian Tour.
earlyRevenueModel: Paid ticket events from day one (~$35 AUD per ticket). Free community swim club (Cold Nips) was a separate pre-existing venture that built community but was never the revenue model.

name: 9D Breathwork (Brian Kelly)
finding: 9D Breathwork's PRIMARY revenue model was always facilitator certification fees, not free public sessions. Brian Kelly discovered breathwork + music while working as a partner in a spiritual tattoo studio in Bali. He co-founded Breath Masters first, then built 9D Breathwork on top of it (~2020-2022, emerged in UK). The model is essentially a DIGITAL FRANCHISE: ~$5,000 upfront certification + mandatory $200/month subscription to access the journey library and use the 9D brand (~$7,400 year one). Facilitators get referral commissions (16.67% on kits, 10% on monthly subs). The 9D website DOES offer free guided sessions and masterclass content online as lead generation for the certification funnel, and the breathing technique itself is free, but the nine-layer audio experience is paid. Public sessions run $25-60 group, $150-250 private. The user's belief is MOSTLY CORRECT: 9D never relied on free events as a business model. Free content exists but only as marketing for the certification pipeline. The early model was paid sessions in Bali, then pivoted to scalable certification/franchise.
earlyRevenueModel: Paid sessions initially (Bali tattoo studio discovery, then Breath Masters certification), then scaled to franchise-style certification model: $5K upfront + $200/month recurring subscription per facilitator. Free online content exists but only as lead generation for the paid certification funnel.

name: Sanctum (Amsterdam)
finding: Sanctum started in 2020 during the pandemic with FREE Instagram Live sessions from the founders' Amsterdam canal house living room. Co-founders Gabriel Olszewski (ex-Diageo Global Head of Comms for Johnnie Walker) and Luuk Melisse (dance/fitness background, inspired by Alan Watts). Gabriel described the early days as 'raw and intimate, just my partner and I hosting daily sessions on Instagram Live from our Amsterdam canal house living room.' These were 'stripped-back but electric, tapping into something people were yearning for.' They then transitioned to PAID in-person classes at iconic Amsterdam venues (churches, art galleries) using headphones. Current class price is approximately EUR 45 (USD 49, GBP 39). They scaled to ~50 employees, ~30 certified Sanctum Guides, Frequency Festivals (500-3000 people), hotel residencies (SIRO Hotels, Six Senses, De L'Europe, art'otel), the World Economic Forum in Davos, and US expansion via Othership NYC. So the early Amsterdam events WERE free (Instagram Live during lockdown), then transitioned to paid in-person headphone classes.
earlyRevenueModel: Started FREE (daily Instagram Live sessions from canal house living room during 2020 pandemic). Transitioned to PAID in-person headphone classes at iconic venues (~EUR 45/class). Revenue now comes from: paid classes, Frequency Festivals (500-3000 attendees), luxury hotel residencies/partnerships, digital app, and corporate events (Davos WEF).

name: Envision Festival (Costa Rica)
finding: Envision was ALWAYS a paid ticket festival from the very first year in 2011. Co-founded by Stephen Brooks (American ethnobotanist, lifelong Burner since 2001, living in Costa Rica since 1995), Josh Wendel, and Brendan Jeffer (Danyasa Yoga Studio). The origin was a festival wedding on raw land in 2010, which inspired them to do a proper festival. First year (2011) in Dominical had 600-700 attendees. Early bird tickets were $150 (confirmed via Envision Festival Facebook post from early years). The festival was inspired by Burning Man but was NOT donation-based like Burning Man. It was always a ticketed, paid-entry festival. Grew from ~600-700 (year 1) to ~6,000 (year 5, sold out days before gates opened) to ~7,000+ (year 11). Currently tickets range $350-$1,200 for VIP. The user's current categorization as 'small group paid' is CORRECT for the early days. It was a small (600-700 person) paid festival that scaled up steadily.
earlyRevenueModel: Paid ticket festival from day one. Early bird tickets ~$150 in the first years. Started with 600-700 attendees in Dominical. Revenue from ticket sales, with the festival held on raw/borrowed land initially (festival wedding venue, then behind Danyasa yoga studio). Not donation-based like Burning Man despite the Burner inspiration.
